readyme.title: ReadyMe
readyme.subtitle: Redesigning a learning app end to end
readyme.lead: ReadyMe helps Sri Lankan students prepare for their G.C.E. A/L exams through structured learning paths built by tutors. I led a complete redesign of the live app, from the information architecture and flows to every screen and a new design system, turning a dense, subject-first app into a calm, discovery-led learning experience.
challenge: The original app worked, but it was built around a list of exam subjects. Students landed on a wall of similar cards, with a large subscribe banner competing for attention and no sense of what to study next.

Screens were dense: stats tiles, long topic tables, boxed answer options and several competing primary actions. Each flow looked slightly different, which made the product feel heavier than it needed to.
goals: Help students find the right learning path, tutor and content, instead of starting from a list of subjects.
Clear hierarchy, more whitespace and one obvious primary action per screen.
A design system of tokens and reusable components so every flow feels like the same product.

pairs.title: Home
points: “My Subjects” list replaced by a Discover feed: latest learning paths, featured tutors and exam-prep rows
Rich path cards with tutor, rating, language and subject tags
Subscribe banner removed from the main view; a four-tab bar (Discover, Activity, My paths, Account) gives clear entry points

pairs.title: Choosing what to learn

Each path shows its tutor, rating and tags, so students can compare at a glance

pairs.title: Course page
points: Stats tiles and a long topics table replaced by a focused hub
Four clear destinations: Learning materials, Analytics, Chat with tutor and Leaderboard
“New content” badge highlights what changed since the last visit

pairs.title: Answering questions

Image-led questions get room to breathe, with Quick ref one tap away
Answers move to their own view, toggled from a single bottom control

pairs.title: Choosing an answer
points: Boxed A/B/C/D options became full-sentence choices that are easier to read
One clear primary action, Submit, instead of a dark Next bar
Previous / next and Question toggle stay in the same place on every question

pairs.title: Login
points: Warmer welcome and a simpler, left-aligned form
Google, Facebook and Apple sign-in as a compact row instead of full-width buttons
Clear “Create an account” path at the bottom

pairs.title: Plans & paywall

The plan choice is the only decision on the screen

Improved type hierarchy for headlines, subheadings and body text
Whitespace and contrast used to highlight what matters
Reusable cards, buttons, inputs and progress indicators

glance: The app was organised around a fixed list of exam subjects. Students landed on near-identical cards, a permanent subscribe banner and no clear next step.
I audited every flow, rebuilt the navigation around learning, and designed a component system so every screen shares the same patterns and hierarchy.
A discovery-first home, a clear course hub, a calmer question flow and one consistent visual language across iOS, iPad and web.

screens in the new light theme, plus a full dark theme
core flows rebuilt end to end
main tabs, each with one clear job
audiences: Preparing for their G.C.E. A/L exams on the ReadyMe app and web.
Find the right learning path and tutor quickly
See progress and know what to do next
Build and publish learning paths and question sets in the authoring tool.
Have their content presented clearly and credibly
Show ratings, language and subject at a glance
audit: Subject-first entry
Home opened on a fixed list of exam subjects, so there was nothing to discover and no sense of what to do next.
Dense, all-caps metadata
Exam name, provider and plan were squeezed into small all-caps lines that were hard to scan.
Repetitive cards
Every subject card repeated the same two counters, so nothing stood out or invited a tap.
Floating button over content
A floating action button sat on top of the list and covered part of a card.
Paywall before value
A subscribe banner was pinned to the home screen before students had experienced any content.
Navigation not built for learning
One of three main tabs went to Settings, while finding and continuing learning had no clear home.
principles: Lead with content students want, and ask for a subscription only once they've seen its value.
Clear hierarchy, generous whitespace and a single obvious primary action on every screen.
Tokens and reusable components, so every flow feels like the same product and ships faster.

authoring.title: ReadyMe Authoring Tool
authoring.subtitle: A calmer workspace for tutors
authoring.lead: The authoring tool is where tutors build everything students see in ReadyMe: learning paths, question sets, notes, videos and study decks. I led its redesign alongside the student app, turning a metrics-heavy dashboard into a content-first workspace with guided creation flows.
glance: Tutors opened the tool to a wall of metrics and an unlabeled icon sidebar. Creating content, their main job, had no clear starting point, and long forms asked for everything at once.
I reorganised the tool around the tutor's real work: one hub for every content type, guided step-by-step creation, and a review step before anything is published.
A labelled side menu, a teaching resources hub, a 3-step learning path flow, faster question creation from PDFs and images, and a review & publish step.
stats: desktop screens in the original tool, reviewed flow by flow
desktop screens designed for the new tool
content types in one resources hub
guided steps to create a learning path
audit: Icon-only navigation
The sidebar had three unlabeled icons, so tutors had to guess where paths, content and settings lived.
Banner competing with the work
A large decorative verification banner was the most prominent element on the home screen.
The same numbers twice
Account-wide stats and the path-level stats below repeated learners, question sets and earnings.
Unclear number formatting
Values such as “.50,000” had no currency and were hard to read at a glance.
Metrics first, content second
Home was all reporting; there was no clear starting point for creating paths, questions or notes.
